title_en: Apple TV Is Bringing Back One of Its Best Shows in August, Three Years After Fans Thought It Ended
body_en:
The surprise return of Ted Lasso is definitely the biggest premiere on Apple TV this August, but we’re also going to get some decent variety from the quality-over-quantity service. There’s an adorable animated series for the kids, a new sports doc, and, of course, plenty of sci-fi.
You can check out what’s premiering on the service in August below, or jump ahead to the full release schedule (which includes continuing series like Silo Season 3 and Sugar Season 2 ) by day.
Ted Lasso is officially entering its fourth season. You might be thinking, didn’t Ted (Jason Sudeikis) go home in a pretty conclusive ending to Season 3? Well now he’s back in Richmond to coach a second division women’s football team. Naturally, there will still be plenty of familiar faces, including Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), Roy (Brett Goldstein), and Keeley (Juno Temple), coming along for the ride.
This crime thriller series takes place in the 70s, when four Mexican women who are used by a police force to distract from a serial killer decide to put in the work to try and crack the case. Also known as Las Azules, the series is theoretically inspired by real events.
One of Apple TV’s few animated children’s shows is coming back for a fifth season. Stillwater is based on Jon J. Muth’s book series Zen, which tells stories of siblings who learn life lessons from their neighbor, Stillwater the panda.
The only documentary addition for the month, The Dynasty: UConn Huskies will trace 40 years of women’s basketball history at the University of Connecticut. The three-part series will cover the team’s time with head coach Geno Auriemma, which saw them win 12 national championships.
Dark Matter is an adaptation of a reality-bending book by Blake Crouch. In the words of Samantha Nelson, who reviewed the first season for IGN , “It’s a tale of a protagonist so desperate to get back the people they love that they'll tear down the walls between realities.” Season 2 will continue to follow the Dessen family and the consequences of tearing down some of those multidimensional walls.
Aside from Stillwater and the UConn Huskies documentary, every Apple TV series will release new episodes each week. In a very satisfying turn of events, every new addition to Apple TV in August will be on Wednesdays and Fridays.
Apple TV continues to keep things simple (stupid) with a single subscription plan . For $12.99/month or $99.99/year, you get access to all things Apple TV without ever getting any ads. It's also one of the last surviving streaming services to still offer a free trial .
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
